phases.name: Walking skeleton: ticket submission through automatic classification (US-01 + US-02)

steps.name: Ticket submission triggers automatic classification with a stated rationale (WS-1)
steps.criteria: POST /api/tickets accepts a title and description and returns 201 with a real ticket id; running the classification step against a fake LLM response of DEVELOPMENT_WORK causes GET /api/tickets/:id to report classificationResult = DEVELOPMENT_WORK and a classificationRationale that reflects the stated reason; the full path (create ticket, classify, read result) runs through the real Hono app and real SQLite, with only the Classifier's generate() call faked -- deleting the real HTTP/DB adapters would break this test.
steps.scenario_name: Maria submits a ticket and sees it classified as development work with a rationale

phases.name: Ticket intake hardening: validation, idempotency, dashboard, multi-source reuse (US-01, US-11)

steps.name: Ticket intake validation and duplicate-submission idempotency
steps.criteria: POST /api/tickets with a blank title returns 400 with a non-empty error message and creates no ticket row; two POST /api/tickets requests carrying the same idempotencyKey return the same ticket id (first response 201, second response 200) and the dashboard list contains exactly one row for that id, never two.
steps.scenario_name: A ticket submission without a title is rejected; Duplicate submission with the same idempotency key does not create a second ticket record

steps.name: Low-detail flagging, dashboard visibility, and multi-source intake reuse
steps.criteria: A ticket submitted with only a title (no description) is created successfully (201) with isLowDetail = true; a submitter's previously created ticket appears in the list returned by GET /api/tickets; a ticket submitted with source = TRELLO and a sourceRef reuses the same POST /api/tickets endpoint, returns 201 with an id in the TICKET-{n} format, and is otherwise indistinguishable downstream from a native-form ticket (ADR-0009).
steps.scenario_name: A ticket with no description is still accepted and flagged as low-detail; Submitted tickets are visible in the submitter's ticket dashboard list; A Trello-sourced ticket reuses the native intake endpoint and is indistinguishable downstream (ADR-0009)

phases.name: Classification decision logic: judgment paths, confirmation gate, failure handling (US-02)

steps.name: Classifier judgment paths: content-only and ambiguous tickets
steps.criteria: Given a fake LLM response of NOT_DEVELOPMENT_WORK for a content-only ticket, the ticket's classificationResult becomes NOT_DEVELOPMENT_WORK and its rationale routes the submitter toward the right team; given a fake LLM response of LOW_CONFIDENCE for a genuinely ambiguous ticket, the ticket's classificationResult becomes LOW_CONFIDENCE and no confirming audit entry is ever recorded for it.
steps.scenario_name: A content-only ticket is classified away from development work, with a routing suggestion; An ambiguous ticket produces a low-confidence result and does not unblock implementation

steps.name: Structural gate: LOW_CONFIDENCE and NOT_DEVELOPMENT_WORK never unblock implementation
steps.criteria: For both LOW_CONFIDENCE and NOT_DEVELOPMENT_WORK classification results, regardless of rationale content, the ticket's classificationResult is never DEVELOPMENT_WORK and ticket.classification.confirmed is never emitted -- the gating rule holds as a structural, provable property of the decision boundary, not an incidental outcome of particular test data, satisfying US-02 AC5 (brief.md's stated #2 quality-attribute priority for this track).
steps.scenario_name: LOW CONFIDENCE and NOT DEVELOPMENT WORK results never unblock implementation, regardless of rationale content

steps.name: Classification failure handling: LLM error and unparseable response
steps.criteria: When the injected generate() call rejects (an LLM error), the ticket's classificationStatus becomes FAILED and classificationFailureReason names the failure -- never left PENDING; when generate() returns a response that is not valid JSON or not one of the three enum values, the ticket is likewise surfaced as classificationStatus = FAILED, with classificationResult never coerced into one of the three valid guessed values.
steps.scenario_name: Classification failure (LLM error) is surfaced, never silently left pending; Classifier returns an unparseable response — treated identically to an LLM failure, never coerced

steps.name: Redelivery no-op and infrastructure-failure handling for classification
steps.criteria: Re-running the classification step for an already-classified ticket leaves its audit-history length and classificationResult unchanged (no duplicate audit row is written); HttpTicketRepository's recordClassification call rejects (never silently swallows) when the underlying HTTP call fails with a network error; a generate() call that times out results in classificationStatus = FAILED, never left PENDING.
steps.scenario_name: A redelivered ticket.created for an already-classified ticket is a no-op; HttpTicketRepository surfaces a network failure from the classification-recording call, never silently swallowed; A Classifier generate() timeout is treated as a classification failure, not left pending

steps.name: Governance override unblocks a misclassified ticket (WS-2)
steps.criteria: POST /api/tickets/:id/override, called by the ticket's own submitter, updates classificationResult to the requested value and returns 200, with the audit history recording the from/to transition; the same route, called by a human who is a governance-team member but not the submitter, likewise succeeds (200) and the resulting audit entry records that governance member's id as the actor -- covering both authorized-actor paths named in US-03.
steps.scenario_name: Devon overrides a misclassified ticket and implementation becomes unblocked; Priya (a governance-team member who is not the submitter) can override, and the override is audited with her identity

steps.name: Override authorization, redelivery idempotency, and reversal
steps.criteria: POST /api/tickets/:id/override from a human who is neither the submitter nor a governance-team member returns 403 and writes no audit row; an identical override action submitted a second time leaves the audit-history length unchanged (no duplicate row, no duplicate confirmation event); a governance override back to NOT_DEVELOPMENT_WORK updates classificationResult accordingly and is audited without re-triggering ticket.classification.confirmed.
steps.scenario_name: Override is rejected for a human who is neither the submitter nor a governance-team member; A redelivered identical override action is a no-op; A governance override back to NOT DEVELOPMENT WORK is audited without re-triggering implementation

steps.name: Governance audit trail visibility
steps.criteria: GET /api/tickets/:id/classification-history returns the ticket's full decision sequence in order (initial classification, then override), with each entry exposing eventType, fromResult, toResult, actorId, and createdAt -- satisfying US-03 AC4's who/when/from/to requirement for governance review.
steps.scenario_name: The override audit trail records who, when, from, and to, visible to governance review
